summary: The sole spec repo has no CI running buf lint/breaking or any gherkin parse/ID check.
EventRequest.route_to_handler is documented default true but is a proto3 bool (false), so callers that omit it bypass HandleFact; the skip_handler fix exists only as core's staged edit.

COMMUTATIVE (the default, wire 0) behaves as STRICT: pre-validation rejects any mismatch with retryable FAILED_PRECONDITION before load, the field-diff reflection pool is only initialised in the status bin, and the spec itself contradicts types.proto on what COMMUTATIVE means; MANUAL never reaches its DLQ for client commands.

The saga/PM sequencing model is undecided: saga.proto says the framework stamps angzarr_deferred, features require clients to stamp explicit sequences (erasing rejection provenance in the same oneof), and core never populates destination_sequences so basis_seq is always 0.

Two main-timeline sentinels ("" and "angzarr"): Bigtable/Dynamo/ImmuDB write under "" but read main as "angzarr", so aggregate replay returns empty history and the next write conflicts forever; the spec itself names both.

Compensator responses are merged inconsistently: client-rust keeps only Events so the documented delegate_to_framework Revocation is dropped, and the router returns one compensator verbatim but drops escalations with two or more; no spec defines the merge.
scaffold names the stub type after the anchor message when no component name is set (every saga, incl. canonical TableHandSaga), which does not compile in Go/Java/C#/C++; lint does not catch it.
About 10 client-rust step worlds never call the library (self-satisfying asserts, empty Thens), including coordinator-contract simulations the spec README says no suite executes.

DeclareAction writes amount_to_call where the applier expects an absolute current_bet (a declared raise lowers current_bet); the proto never defines ActionTaken.amount semantics and scenarios contradict each other.
angzarr-project is not the sole source: core owns dlq_admin.proto and diverged copies of 13 feature files, and prj-cloudevents compiles a package-rewritten local copy of cloudevents.proto.
16 removed field numbers are commented but not reserved (core's staged fix still misses AngzarrDeadLetter 4-6).
No scenario covers 2PC, DECISION/ISOLATED/CASCADE, CascadeErrorMode, DLQ, MERGE_MANUAL, SnapshotRetention, EventStream or descriptors; deleted sync_modes/poker_game features are still cited.
Coordinator-contract errors: fact_flow expects 1-based sequences (4/5 instead of 3/4) and a removed Cover.external_id.
Every production snapshot is RETENTION_DEFAULT and no store prunes DEFAULT (Bigtable prunes nothing), so snapshots grow unbounded.
TemporalQuery says no snapshots while Snapshot.created_at says snapshots are used for temporal-by-time.

Rejection delivery transport is unspecified (no rpc takes Notification) and the routing key diverges: options.proto and router key on FQ type, features on (source_domain, command), client-rust on (domain, simple name).
ComponentOptions.output_domain is singular while sagas/PMs target multiple domains.
Poker scenarios are internally wrong: EU-1260 loses 100 chips, EU-1339 contradicts EU-1341, EU-0575 has one player on button and BB.
@EU-0531 is reused 7 times, @EU-1184B..F are malformed and 276/1021 scenarios have no ID.
Example protos emit into the client-go module path, coupling the framework client to poker.
Poker spec nits: missing tournament statuses, wrong TDA rule citations, weak/impossible scenarios.
Spec tier nits: poker vocabulary in client tier, client tier needs a backend, client naming drift.
Framework proto doc nits: SyncMode order omits ISOLATED, cascade_id comment names wrong field, orphan GetDescriptor messages, stale sererr comment.
READMEs and examples-rust still cite deleted poker_game/sync_modes features; @wip left on EA-0004.
History/ticket commentary in protos, features and core code violates the no-change-commentary rule.
